new_findings_today.title: Business Report persona-leak (NEW-2026-08-14-005) needed two attempts to actually close -- the first, data-only fix looked plausible but was verified insufficient by reading the output, not by re-reading the code
new_findings_today.detail: The first fix attempt this session (a short run.executor + a business_summary object) was based on a partial reading of qa/_lib/build_report.js that correctly identified header()'s raw run.executor line as A leak vector but missed that buildBusiness() also unconditionally rendered new_findings_today[].detail, a fully-flattened headline_metrics table, and the raw regression_matrix table -- none of which were gated by business_summary being present. That first attempt would have shipped a Business Report that still leaked commit hashes and file paths, and looked plausible right up until the actual .docx was opened and scanned. The bug is now fixed properly at the source (build_report.js edited, buildDeveloper/buildQA left untouched and confirmed still fully detailed). The general lesson, worth keeping: for a bug in a generator/renderer, reading the generator's source is necessary but reading the SOURCE is not the same as reading the OUTPUT -- always independently verify the actual rendered artifact (here: extract and scan the .docx text) before calling a leak/rendering bug fixed, the same discipline this repo already applies to rendered web pages (see CLAUDE.md's 'verify the RENDERED page, not just the data' rule) and should apply equally to generated documents.
new_findings_today.evidence: First-attempt .docx (before the source fix) contained 7+ commit-hash-like tokens and 20+ file-path-like tokens when regex-scanned, despite business_summary being fully populated and run.executor being short. Second-attempt .docx (after editing buildBusiness() in qa/_lib/build_report.js) scanned clean: 0 of each.
new_findings_today.recommendation: No further action needed on this specific bug -- closed at the source. Generalize the lesson: any future 'fix' to a report/document generator should be verified by scanning the actual generated file's extracted text, not by re-reading the generator code and reasoning about what it should do.

business_summary.headline: The three biggest open issues from the past week — the map that wasn't showing up on destination and explore pages, the occasional slowdown on the Hindi explore page, and stale numbers in the site's background SEO data — were all fixed and independently checked live today. Nothing new and urgent came up.
context: This is one in a running series of daily, fully-automated health checks of nakshiq.com that has been going since early May 2026 — every check in this report was performed live against the real site today, not estimated or carried over from a prior day.

The three fixes below were shipped by an earlier work session yesterday evening and had not yet been independently confirmed working until today's check. All three are now confirmed: measured directly (e.g. checking exactly where a map pin appears on screen, not just that the map loaded), not just assumed from the description of the fix.

The value of checking daily rather than only when a visitor reports a problem is visible in today's results: the Hindi Explore page slowdown had been intermittently recurring for 11 weeks before it was properly fixed, but because it only ever affected a fraction of visits, it's the kind of issue that's easy to miss without a systematic daily check — and easy to mistake as 'fixed' after a fix ships, without directly confirming it, which is exactly what today's session caught a gap in from a prior day's report.
traffic_lights: All 32 core pages checked loaded successfully; 10/10 sampled destination pages loaded correctly in both English and Hindi.
Fixed today. The map on destination pages and the Explore page now renders correctly — verified by directly measuring where the map pins and tiles appear on screen, not just that the map code ran.
Fixed today. The recurring slow-loading issue on the Hindi Explore page is resolved — zero slowdowns recorded in the 16+ hours since the fix went out, versus a recurring pattern before.
Fixed today. The site's structured data (used by search engines and AI tools) now shows the correct, current destination and verdict counts instead of an out-of-date number.

All sampled pages show correct Hindi language tags, titles, and section headings. One narrower, known gap continues: on a subset of destination pages, the main heading itself still shows in English on the Hindi site — unchanged, tracked separately, not urgent.
Every one of the 533 destinations has emergency contact info on file, well above the safety minimum. No change.
The file search engines use to discover pages (the sitemap) is complete and unchanged: roughly 25,000 URLs covering all 533 destinations. No pages have quietly disappeared from it.

The overnight job that keeps hotel and stay recommendations current ran successfully again, refreshing recommendations for 20 destinations. It correctly declined to write a recommendation for one destination rather than invent one.
One subscriber from the first newsletter send (4+ days ago) still shows no delivery confirmation of any kind. Worth a direct look at the email platform's dashboard.

A recurring daily automation (the analytics-audit job) again failed to save its own work automatically and needed a manual assist today — the 3rd+ time this specific hiccup has happened this week. Nothing broken for site visitors; it just means someone should look at why this keeps needing a manual nudge.
whats_changed: Fixed: the map on destination pages (like Betla) and the Explore page — pins and map tiles were rendering thousands of pixels off-screen, making the map area look blank. Now confirmed rendering correctly in the right place.
Fixed: the map's background imagery provider was returning a broken 'API key required' placeholder image. Switched to a different free map provider (Esri) — confirmed working.

Fixed: the Hindi version of the Explore page was occasionally timing out under load. The underlying database query was restructured to load once and cache, instead of running fresh (and slow) on every visit.
Fixed: the site's background SEO data (used by search engines and AI assistants to understand the site) was quoting an old, smaller destination count. Now shows the live, correct number.
Fixed: a small housekeeping gap from a week ago (a QA report's supporting files never got saved to the project) has been cleaned up.
The site's automatic map imagery is now the same for all destination pages, the Explore page, and the trekking-trail pages — all three were checked today and all three work correctly.
risks: One newsletter recipient from last week's first-ever send still shows zero delivery confirmation after 4+ days — worth checking the email platform's dashboard directly rather than waiting longer.

A recurring analytics housekeeping task keeps failing to save its own daily output automatically, needing a manual rescue most days this week. Not customer-facing, but worth a permanent fix so it stops needing daily attention.

A background job that keeps hotel/stay recommendations current still can't fully double-check its own work due to a technical network restriction in its automated environment — it has a reliable backup check in place, but a permanent fix would remove the need for that workaround.
bottom_line: No action needed on the site itself today — the three fixes shipped yesterday evening are confirmed working.
Worth 5 minutes: check the Resend (email) dashboard for why one newsletter subscriber shows no delivery signal after 4+ days.

Worth a decision at some point (not urgent): either fix the daily analytics-audit automation so it stops needing a manual save each day, or accept that a human/QA session will keep doing it and stop treating it as a problem to solve.
tomorrow: Tomorrow's check will re-confirm all three of today's fixes are still holding, sample a fresh 10 random destinations, and check whether the newsletter delivery gap for the one silent subscriber has resolved or needs a more direct look.

It will also check whether the daily analytics-audit automation saved its own work without needing a manual assist — three or more days in a row of it needing help is the signal that this needs a permanent fix rather than a daily workaround.

business_about_this_report.note: How this report gets made, for context:
items: This check runs on a daily schedule without anyone needing to trigger it by hand. It visits the live site the same way a real visitor would — loading pages, following links, and reading what actually comes back — rather than just checking that the underlying code looks correct.

Every number in this report comes from something measured today: a page that was actually loaded, a database query that was actually run, or a screen that was actually looked at. Nothing here is estimated or copied forward from a previous day without being re-checked.

Three versions of this report are produced from the same underlying checks: this plain-language version for a business owner, a more detailed version for whoever is doing QA review, and a fully technical version for whoever is fixing things day-to-day. All three describe the same day's findings, just at different levels of detail for different readers.

When something can't be checked for a good reason (for example, a check that would require submitting a real form, or a deeper review that's simply not due yet), that's stated plainly rather than skipped silently or guessed at.

This report and the two more technical companion reports are all regenerated from a single underlying set of today's results — none of the three re-runs any checks or re-measures anything independently, they simply present the same day's findings for three different readers.
If a number in this report looks surprising, the more detailed companion reports break every section down further, section by section, with the specific evidence behind each pass or fail.
